title: Same energy, different tariff
hook: Moving to a cheaper tariff: do you use less energy?

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Distinguish a cost change from an energy-use change.

misconception: A lower electricity charge necessarily means fewer kilowatt-hours were used.
objective: Distinguish a cost change from an energy-use change.

claims.text: For a stated constant load, kWh = watts × hours ÷ 1000. Running cost = kWh × the stated price per kWh; stated fixed costs are added separately.
claims.source: https://www.energy.gov.au/households/energy-rating Australian Government, Energy Ratings, sections Electrical appliances without a star rating / Estimate running costs. Opened 2026-10-13. This supports the general calculation, not the invented model ratings or tariff. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Verified as a derivation from unit definitions, not on the cited energy.gov.au page (not opened). Energy (Wh) = power (W) × time (h), and 1 kWh = 1000 Wh, so kWh = W × h ÷ 1000 for a constant load; a per-kWh price is by definition charged per kWh, so energy cost = kWh × price, and any stated fixed charge is a separate term. Matches the stage formulas printed by resourceFormula (e.g. 3 kWh × €0.40 = €1.20 and × €0.20 = €0.60).
